frontier.hypothesis: A byte-free fifth block-local allocno exists - a pseudo that receives a hard register at local-alloc and whose defining insn is deleted afterwards - and can be combined with a byte-free pointer use after it.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc assigns block-local quantities ascending (v0,v1,a0,a1,a2) BEFORE global.c allocates the pointer, so only deletions that happen after local-alloc (reload, jump2/cross_jump, delay-slot fill in reorg.c, final.c) can leave the seat occupied at allocation time and empty in the emitted bytes.
